text: A run whose tracked work has all settled and whose engine then goes quiet ends on the grace window **silently**: it emits no `warning` and no `error` about the hold, and its last event is its `result`. Settled work plus a quiet engine is the normal end of a task-touching run, not a truncation — announcing it would fire on the happy path of every run that so much as spawned a subagent. This is the grace bound's half of the asymmetry: only the hard cap, which can expire only with work genuinely unsettled and the engine still alive, ends the run with a terminal error.
title: A run whose tracked work has all settled and whose engine then goes quiet ends on the grace window silently — no warning and no error; its last event is its result
